correctness.rationale: The minimum-Rayleigh-quotient characterization proves concavity on the fixed constant-vector complement, so a wheel rotation average suffices for the value. Nonnegative uniform spokes attain positive value, and homogeneity forces budget exhaustion. The radial eigenvalue is (n+1)x and the first rim Fourier eigenvalue is x+α_n y, including n=3. Their minimum along the budget line is maximized at the crossing when Q<α_n P, at the star endpoint when Q>α_n P, and on the displayed interval when equal. An optimal averaged minimum eigenvector must also be a minimum eigenvector of any design realizing that average: the Rayleigh remainders are nonnegative and average to zero. In the star regime the vanishing average forces every rim weight to vanish; hub equations on rim differences then force equal spokes. In the crossing regime the radial vector forces equal spokes, and the first complex mode forces the flux differences around the cycle to be constant. Consecutive phases are not real multiples, so the real conductance deviations must vanish. This proves exactly the claimed uniqueness scope, not an assertion about asymmetric equality designs. The equal-price cases follow from α_6=1 and strict decrease, and n²α_n→4π² gives the stated critical-window limit including the crossover. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed.
